options.label: D
options.text: force of attraction or repulsion depends upon speed of beams.

questions._flag: Official key kept as printed, but recorded as a disagreement for a human. Electron and proton beams travelling the same way constitute ANTIPARALLEL conventional currents, so the magnetic force between them is repulsive - which is the reasoning option (b) rewards. The charges are however OPPOSITE, so the Coulomb force is attractive, and at non-relativistic beam speeds it exceeds the magnetic force by roughly \((c/v)^2\), making the net force attractive. The item is answerable only if the magnetic interaction is read as the one being asked about.
